transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because this has gotten kind of out of hand. In the summer especially, I plan so much of what I do around avoiding wasps. I’ve stopped doing the garden jobs at church, and if I hear buzzing near the back porch, I make my husband unload things instead of going out there myself. It’s just starting to run things more than I want it to.
Do you ever have panic or feel like you're going to have a panic attack when you see a wasp or think you might see one?

Yes, pretty much right away. If I hear that sharp buzzing by the porch or see one hanging around the flowers, my heart jumps and my hands start shaking. I just feel like I need to get inside immediately.
Do you also fear other insects like bees or hornets, or is it mainly just wasps that cause this reaction?

It’s mainly wasps. I mean, I don’t like bees or hornets either, but wasps are the ones that really set me off. I know they’re just little insects and other people might just swat them away, but to me, if one gets near me, it feels like something awful is about to happen.
Are there other situations or objects, besides wasps, that you avoid because they cause you significant fear or anxiety?
Not really, no. I can’t think of anything else that I avoid in that same way. It’s mostly the wasps.
Is your fear of wasps mainly because you're afraid of being stung by them?
Yes, mostly. I mean, I know it’s just a little insect and most people would just swat it away, but if a wasp gets close to me, it feels like something terrible is about to happen.
How long have you been afraid of wasps?
It started after we had some remodeling done and they uncovered a wasp nest. That was about two years and five months ago. Since then, I’ve been afraid of them.
Has your fear of wasps affected your relationships or work in any significant way?

Yes, it has. I’m not working, so it hasn’t affected a job, but socially it has. I’ve stepped back from the church gardening group, and I don’t host garden days anymore like I used to. That was one of the main ways I stayed connected with people.

At home, my husband does the porch and garden stuff now that I used to take care of myself. So it’s not ruining everything, but it has changed things.
How much of your daily life would you say is affected by your fear of wasps?

A fair amount, I’d say. It’s mostly the things outside or around the garden. I’ve stopped doing the church gardening group, and I don’t host those garden days anymore, which used to be a big way I saw people. At home, my husband handles the porch and garden chores now, things I used to do myself. So it’s not every minute of the day, but it has definitely changed my routine.
Have you ever avoided going outside at all during the summer because of your fear of wasps?

Yes. I don’t always stay inside completely, but in the summer I plan a lot around avoiding them. If I hear buzzing near the back porch, I’ll avoid going out there, and I’ll even have my husband unload things instead. I’ve also given up the garden jobs at church because I just don’t want to be out there dealing with wasps.
Would you say your avoidance of wasps has caused you significant distress?

Yes, it has. That’s really why I’m here. I’ve gotten to where I plan my whole summer around avoiding wasps. I gave up my garden jobs at church, and if I hear buzzing by the back porch, I’ll make my husband unload things instead of going out there myself. It’s upsetting, because it feels like it’s running more of my life than it should.
Is your fear of wasps more about the wasp itself or the possibility of it stinging you?

It’s more the sting, I think, but also just the wasp being near me. I know it’s a tiny insect and other people might just swat it away, but when one gets close, I feel like something awful is about to happen.
Have you avoided social gatherings or events because of your fear of encountering wasps?

Yes. I’ve avoided some things, especially in the summer. I’ve already stopped doing the garden jobs at church because I don’t want to be out there around wasps. And even at home, if I hear buzzing near the back porch, I’ll ask my husband to handle things instead of going out there myself. It’s gotten to where I plan around it more than I’d like.
Have you avoided spending time with friends or family because of your fear of wasps?

Yes, I have. In the summer especially, I’ll avoid being outside with people if I think wasps might be around. I’ve even stopped doing the garden work at church, and at home I’ll have my husband go out on the porch or unload things if I hear buzzing. It feels like I’m planning everything around not running into them.
Have you avoided intimate relationships or physical closeness with your husband due to your fear of wasps?
I don’t think so. I mean, not physical closeness with my husband in general. It’s more about avoiding places or situations where I think wasps might be around.
Have you lost any friends because of your fear of wasps?

I don’t think I’ve lost friends outright, no. But I have stepped back from things that kept me connected, like the church gardening group, and I stopped hosting garden days at my house. So I haven’t lost people exactly, but I do see them less because of it. At home, my husband has taken over the porch and garden things I used to do myself.
Is your fear of wasps only about the possibility of being stung by them, or is there another aspect of wasps that frightens you?

It’s mostly the stinging, I think, but it’s more than just a normal worry about that. I know it’s just a little insect and other people might swat it away, but if one gets near me, I feel like something awful is about to happen. It just sets off this panic in me.
Is there anything about wasps that frightens you other than the possibility of being stung by them?

Not really anything specific besides the sting. It’s just that when a wasp gets close, even though I know it’s small and most people would just swat it away, I feel like something terrible is about to happen.
Is your fear of wasps only about the pain or harm that their sting could cause you?

It’s mainly about the sting, yes, but it feels bigger than just the pain. I know a wasp is tiny and most people would just brush it away, but if one gets near me, I feel like something terrible is about to happen.
Is your fear of wasps' sting only about the physical pain it could cause you?
No, it’s not just the pain. I mean, I know it’s only a little insect and most people would just swat it away, but if one comes near me, I feel like something really terrible is about to happen.
